# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers say the schedule and getting subs to show up is what really eats the day, so one group named in plain site words is exactly how a super would sort them.
whys.g2: There is no junk, explicit or off-topic answer on this line, so nothing needed keeping out.

founder.order_why: It runs context, then problem, then delivery, and the recall window sitting between the two context screens reads as part of defining the moment, so nothing felt out of place.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the identical question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.'), so it looks like the same context screen shown twice; the check screens 11/12 and 14/15 also show the Importance and Current-solution rows a second time after the review, which reads as a repeat unless it is clear what changed.
founder.missing: Nothing about my solution (narrated short videos on the walk turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC), my price ($1k per site per month), or that the general contractor pays rather than the superintendent, so the buyer and the willingness to pay are never asked in this flow.

PRIMARY.order_why: It asks me which part I'd most like made easier before asking how my last daily log actually went, so I'm picking a wish before I've walked back through the day; the how-it-went screen should come first.
PRIMARY.asked_twice: Screens 2 and 3 overlap a little: 'did you finish the log after hours' then 'on how many days', though I can see the second just counts the first.
PRIMARY.missing: Nothing about the photos: how many I took through the day, or the hours it takes uploading and tagging them in Procore, which is the slowest part of my log. Also nothing about why the log has to be right, like using it later in a dispute with the owner over delays. Screen 5 also assumes I type it up in the trailer, but a lot of mine gets done from the truck or at home.

screens.why7: The own row is first and whole, with four rivals in a nine-word, -ing shape, and the belief can be both supported and refuted; but the sub-attendance row is a part of the own row, which the card forbids.
screens.instead: Keep the list but restore the sub row as 'Lining up subs to show up tomorrow' so it is no longer a piece of the daily log.

screens.why1: Right after the problem's importance, asking how supers handle the log today is the obvious next question, and it is the fourth of four problem screens as the frame says.
screens.why2: "How do they deal with it today?" is plain to me, since "it" is the daily log after the walks from the screens just before; the hint's example "checking for errors by hand" is from another trade but only an example.
screens.why3: I know exactly how my supers do it: photos on the walk, then upload and type the log in the trailer, and how long that takes them.
screens.why4: Two boxes for the act and how it goes, and "I'm not sure" is the right founder-side escape for leaving the dimension out.
screens.why5: Both boxes are my own words, kept as typed: the photos, the upload, the trailer, and my three time rungs.
screens.why7: My answer fits the card's shape (the act and its means within 25 words, three rungs on one time measure in typed order), but the hint asks only for the act and never for the second box's rungs or where good enough ends, so my answer marks no acceptable rung and the line falls under the first by default; the act also strings three steps (photo, upload, type) where the card wants the one step that hurts.
screens.instead: First box: "The one step that hurts, and what they do it with, e.g. typing the daily log from the walk photos in the trailer." Second box: "How it goes, best to worst, and say which is still good enough, e.g. Typed up within half an hour of the walk (fine); Took about an hour in the trailer; Took a couple of hours after the walk."

screens.why1: Right after I said how supes handle the log today, Keel asks me to check the five outcomes it will show them, which is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Walk, trailer, typed up and written up are how supers talk about the daily log, so every rung reads plain on first pass.
screens.why3: Every super knows how long the log took after their last walk, so it is answerable from their own day.
screens.why4: The five run cleanly from half an hour to never done that day, each is one clause, none overlap, and every true answer falls on one rung.
screens.why5: My hours-after-the-walk cost and my own two rungs are kept word for word, and the belief names the trailer typing I described.
screens.why7: All five rungs grade the one measure, time spent after the walk; the first is the way working, the last never got done, and the line under the first leaves 1 against and 4 for, so the belief can go either way.

screens.why1: Right after I typed how supers handle the log today, I get to see the five outcomes Keel will put to strangers and where my line sits, which is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Typed up, the walk, the trailer, the rest of the evening: that is how a super talks about the daily log, so every row reads on first pass.
screens.why3: Every super knows how long the log took after the last walk on a given day, so any of them could answer from their own week.
screens.why4: 'Typed up well after the walk was over' overlaps 'Took a couple of hours' and 'Took the rest of the evening', since both of those are also well after, and the common case of roughly an hour in the trailer has no clear home.
screens.why5: My row 'Took about an hour in the trailer' is gone, replaced by a vaguer 'well after the walk', so the rung the 3-hours-a-day pitch hangs on has drifted.
screens.why7: The scale has a working first rung with the line under it, five rungs from best to never done, and the escape sits apart, but rungs 1 and 2 grade when it was done while rungs 3 and 4 grade how long it took, so the one-measure rule is bent.
screens.instead: Typed up within half an hour of the walk · ┄ line ┄ · Took about an hour in the trailer · Took a couple of hours after the walk · Took the rest of the evening · Never got written up that day

screens.why1: Right before the study goes out, choosing who asks the questions belongs here, after the problem has been checked and before people see it.
screens.why2: The question and hint are plain, but the option 'Lock and record the face Keel preselects' needs a second read: lock what, and record whom?
screens.why3: As the founder I know my supers get texts on their phones and might answer from the truck or the trailer, so I can judge whether a spoken, on-screen interviewer suits them.
screens.why4: The choice I made is worded in Keel's own machinery terms rather than mine, so I'm not sure what I'm agreeing to beyond 'use the default face'.
screens.why5: Nothing here changes what I typed about superintendents or the daily log, and nothing of Fresco leaks to the respondent.
screens.instead: Who should ask your questions? — Keel's suggested interviewer (recommended) / Pick a different face / Text only, no video

screens.why1: Right after choosing who asks the questions, picking how superintendents answer is the obvious next step before sending.
screens.why2: Plain words; as the founder I read 'AI interviewer', 'read and tap' and 'Let them choose' on first pass, and the descriptions say exactly what each means.
screens.why3: I know my supers are on their phones in the truck or trailer, often with noise around, so I can judge whether they'd rather tap or talk to a video.
screens.why4: Three distinct, complete choices (AI voice, text, or both) with no overlap and nothing missing; no escape is needed for a setup choice.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product or roles is reworded here; it only asks about delivery, and my pick 'Read and tap' is offered as typed.

screens.why1: Right after choosing how superintendents answer, deciding who gets the link is the obvious last step before sending.
screens.why2: Plain words a founder reads once: people I know, people found through a search, one link posted to a group.
screens.why3: I know exactly who I'd send it to: the supers I've ridden along with in Napa and the South Bay, by name.
screens.why4: Three distinct, complete ways to reach people, no overlap, and no escape is needed on a choice of channel.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product leaks and my pick of named people is kept as I typed it.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits under the title with the deciding count beside it ('Frequency: 4 counted'), and the card shows '5 needed to call it', so I know the problem stage isn't called because I'm one counted super short, although Importance and Current solution are equally short and only Frequency is named.
screens.why_b2: The tally (4 beliefs, 1 holding, 3 too few, 7 answered) and the Prevalence bar (6 of 7, at the bar) are plain, but the kicker's '4 TO 7 COUNTED' and why 5 of 7 is the floor need a second look.
screens.why_b3: My statement is my own words from the launch, and the beliefs are recognisably mine (the end of the day in the trailer, the daily log), but the Importance line is reworded into Keel's scaffolding ('have five things that are hard') and Prevalence becomes 'finished the daily log after the workday ended' rather than my hours in the trailer.
screens.why_b4: Nothing tells me what to do: no line says to get more superintendents counted on Frequency, Importance and Current solution, or what the Prevalence result means for Fresco; 'What it measures' only explains the method.
screens.why_b5: n=7 is on every line, the three short beliefs are called 'too few' rather than read as a lean, and Prevalence is marked 'at the bar' rather than strong.
screens.instead: Not called yet: 6 of 7 supers did finish the log after hours (right at your 8-in-10 bar, so one answer could flip it), but how often, how much it matters and whether the trailer routine falls short each have 4 counted of 5 needed, so get two or three more supers who walked a live site this week before you read it.

screens.why_b1: The status word 'Holding up' sits right beside '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar', so I see both the verdict and the number that decides it.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 6 for and 1 against across 7 people, with my bar marked at 6 and labelled 'at least 8 in 10', so I can see what is counted, the total and the bar at a glance.
screens.why_b3: Prevalence and 'At least 8 in 10' are mine, but my problem was hours in the trailer typing up the log after the site walks, and 'finished the daily log after the workday ended' reads more like off-the-clock work at home, so it is reworded though recognisable.
screens.why_b4: The So line sends me to the next two cards but never says what scraping the bar exactly means for Fresco, for example that one more No would have sunk it.
screens.why_b5: n=7 stays visible, the screen says 'a small group: a lean, not a call', and it does not call an at-the-bar result strong; the tag 'the most recent time it happened' on a yes/no gate is odd but claims nothing.
screens.instead: Holding up, but only just: 6 of 7 typed up the log after the walks, exactly your bar, and one more No would flip it, so treat it as a lean and check Frequency and Importance before leaning on it.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The strip (4 for, 1 empty, bar at 4 of 5) and the middle answer of 5 read quickly, but the axis starts at a 0 nobody could pick and the legend's 'what you said' vs 'at what you said' made me look twice to see where each of the four sat.
screens.why_b3: It is my 4-to-5-out-of-5 belief and my window, but 'finish the daily log after the workday ended' reads like overtime at home, while what I typed in is the hour or so in the trailer after the site walks; it is close enough that I still recognise it.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is true but generic: it doesn't tell me that all four counted answers were for me, or that one more counted answer at 4 or above would make the belief hold.
screens.why_b5: It keeps n visible, names the two not counted and why, and calls the group 'a lean, not a call' instead of claiming a hold from four people; the stray '— the most recent time it happened' after a count question is odd but claims nothing.
screens.instead: Too few to call: all 4 counted said 4 or 5 of the last 5 working days (middle answer 5); one more counted super at 4 or above holds it, so get one more answer before you lean on this.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits with its deciding number, 4 counted and 5 needed, and the So line repeats it consistently.
screens.why_b2: It is plain that the chart counts 8 picks from 4 people, and my row gets 2 of them, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' next to 'at least 2 in 3' and the marker at 4 took me a second look to see the bar means 4 people out of 5, not 4 picks.
screens.why_b3: The card is titled Importance and the belief line is my study's: five difficulties after the site walks, with writing up the daily log after hours as one of their two.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me to get one more superintendent counted, or that Denise and Ray put the schedule and subs above the log.
screens.why_b5: n is visible and the low count is said, but calling a 2-for, 2-against split 'a lean' suggests a direction the four answers don't have.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of 4 put the log in their two and 2 put the schedule and subs first, an even split, not a lean; one more counted superintendent decides it.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the two agree.
screens.why_b2: The rows, their counts and my line under 'Typed up within half an hour of the walk' read at once, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' against a bar stated as '2 in 3' takes a second look to see that it means the floor of 5 and not my threshold.
screens.why_b3: Typing up the daily log in the trailer and my rung are mine, but 'on commercial jobs' is dropped from my people, and the stem's 'your last daily record' is not my word for the occasion (a site walk, or the daily log).
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say that one more counted superintendent decides it, or that the 3-of-4 lean is toward my belief.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (6 answered, 4 counted, why Hank and Luis were not counted), and the small group is named a lean, not a call, with no claim beyond it.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 counted fell short of 'Typed up within half an hour of the walk', which leans toward your belief; one more counted superintendent at your bar of 5 decides it.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', but the screen never says which way the 4 lean, so I see 2 against and cannot tell how close it came to holding or failing.
screens.why_b3: Importance is my dimension and the belief is recognisably mine, though Keel's 'five things that are hard... one of the two' scaffolding wraps my plain claim that writing up the daily log eats supers' evenings.
screens.why_b4: Nothing on the screen says what two supers putting schedule and sub attendance above the log means for Fresco, such as whether to pitch the scribe on schedule updates and sub follow-up from the walk, or to ask more people.
screens.why_b5: The screen keeps n visible and calls nothing strong, but the group title 'Keeping the schedule and subs showing up' reads like a theme when it rests on two people out of four counted, and the screen does not say so.
screens.why_b6: Denise finishing her log on the tablet before she leaves the gate, and Ray letting the log wait till morning because the deck can't, tell me what my pitch is up against: schedule and sub attendance outrank the log, and some supers already log as they go.

screens.why1: As the opening screener it's obvious why it's asked: the study is for supers whose jobs run on Procore or ACC, so it checks that first.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the platforms I live in every day, and 'jobs you're running now' is how I'd say it myself.
screens.why3: I know exactly which platform each of my jobs runs on, because I'm the one uploading photos and daily logs into it.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers it, and 'any of the jobs' handles the super whose jobs are split between platforms, so nobody is left without an answer.
screens.why5: It names only the platforms in the founder's segment and gives nothing away about the product or what's being built.
screens.why6: It's short, one question, and 'ACC' is said the way we say it on site; 'I'll read 2 options' before a plain yes-or-no is a bit stiff, but it's easy to hold and answer.

screens.why1: Right after confirming my jobs run on Procore or ACC, asking whether I had to finish the daily log after hours this week is the obvious next thing to ask me.
screens.why2: Daily log is my word, and 'finish it after the workday ended' is exactly how I'd say staying late in the trailer to get it done, so I can answer on one read.
screens.why3: I know which nights last week I was still punching photos and notes into the log after the crews left, so I can answer from my own week.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it cleanly, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, though 'daily record' there isn't how I'd say it; I call it the daily log.
screens.why5: It asks about the part that hurts, the log still waiting after the day's walks are done, and nothing about any product or app reaches me.
screens.why6: It's one short sentence with 'Yes or no' after it, easy to answer on one hearing.
screens.why7: The gate asks about the costly act, not the routine: a super who closes out the log on the walk or before leaving truly says No, and one finishing it at night says Yes, so the founder's band can be supported or refuted.

screens.why1: I just said yes to finishing the log after the day was over, so asking how many of those five days it happened is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Daily log, working days, after the workday ended: that's how I'd say it, and I can answer on first read.
screens.why3: I know which nights this week I was still in the trailer, or at the kitchen table, punching photos and notes into Procore.
screens.why4: One button per day from 1 to 5, no zero since I already said yes, and 'I can't recall' kept apart covers the rest.
screens.why5: It asks about my own log and my own evenings, and nothing about anybody's product or plan comes through.
screens.why6: It's short and one question, and 'a number from 1 to 5, or say you can't recall' is easy to hold after one hearing.
screens.why7: Every option counts working days out of the window, from 1 to 5 in order, using the gate's own clause in 8 words with the unit said once and the one escape; whether a button can count against depends on the founder's low, which isn't on this screen.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether and how often I finish the log after the day ends, asking which end-of-day chore I'd most like made easier follows naturally.
screens.why2: Subs, RFIs, the walk and the log are all my words, but 'your last day after the site walks' is a clumsy way to say the end of my last workday and takes a second read.
screens.why3: Every one of these is something I've dealt with at the trailer after the walk this week, even if the PE usually finishes the RFIs I raise.
screens.why4: Chasing sub headcount 'for today's log' is a piece of writing up the daily log, so those two options overlap; the rest are distinct and in my words, and None of these fits.
screens.why5: Writing up the daily log after hours is the pain I'd expect this to be about, and nothing about a product or app comes through.
screens.why6: Five short parallel options and one escape read out cleanly, and 'RFIs' is said aloud on every site, so I could hold the list and answer.
screens.why7: The own row is on the list, not first, with three or more other rows and the escape at the first ask, but the sub-attendance rival is part of the daily log itself, which bends the rule that no rival can be a part of the own row.
screens.instead: Think of your last workday. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Lining up tomorrow's crews and deliveries · Updating the schedule after the walk · Writing up RFIs for issues found on the walk · Writing up the daily log after hours · Following up on safety issues from the walk · None of these

screens.why1: After asking how often I finish the log after hours and what I'd want made easier, asking how the last one actually went is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: I'd answer it, but 'daily record' isn't what we call it (it's the daily or the daily log), and 'after the walk' is unclear because I walk the site several times a day and it doesn't say which walk.
screens.why3: I do the log every day, so I know how the last one went, though plenty of nights I'm typing it on my phone or laptop at home, not in the trailer.
screens.why4: 'Typed up well after the walk was over' overlaps both 'took a couple of hours' and 'took the rest of the evening', and the options switch between when it got done and how long it took.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks; it just asks about getting the log typed up, which is my world.
screens.why6: One short question and five short options I can hold, though hearing 'daily record' and then 'daily log' in the same breath sounds like two different things.
screens.why7: Five rungs run best to worst with a working first rung and outright failure last, but rung 2 is vague and overlaps 3 and 4 on the time measure, and the escape should be 'Someone else did it' because the PE or assistant super often writes the daily.
screens.instead: Think of the last day you did the daily log. How long after your last walk was it finished? Within half an hour; within an hour or two; later that evening at home; not till the next morning; never got written up. Or: someone else did it that day.
